findings.title: Slow cloud or capability handshake at boot + no local save => fresh game starts silently and the first autosave overwrites the cloud save
findings.repro: cd game && node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --wait 2500 --script tools/qa_cr_cloudrace2.mjs (mocked window.claude db: cloud doc money 2222, no local mirror, cloud get takes 2.5 s) -> booted {money:6500, toasts:[]}, after autosave('hidden') cloudMoneyNow 6500, newerCloudSaveLost:true. Variant tools/qa_cr_cloudrace3.mjs: capability handshake (claude.use) takes 1.4 s and the cloud read only 50 ms -> same result (fresh game, cloud overwritten).
findings.expected: A player opening the game on a second device, or after the browser cleared or partitioned localStorage (common for embedded third-party iframes / Safari ITP), gets their cloud game back. At minimum the game must never overwrite an existing cloud save it never loaded.
findings.actual: Boot treats 'cloud did not answer in time' as 'no save', starts the starter family with dirty=true and no message. The next tab-hide / pagehide / new-day autosave replaces the cloud document. Other devices then load this newer (empty) game as the newest save, so progress is lost everywhere.
findings.suspected_cause: main.js:340-354 pickInitialState races M.save.loadEntry against CLOUD_BOOT_WAIT=1500 ms. On timeout with no local mirror it returns {state:null, where:'new'}, and offerNewerCloud is only called when a local save exists (main.js:350). save.js:304 loadEntry waits only INIT_WAIT_LOAD=1200 ms for capabilities and then resolves null (not undefined), so with a slow handshake the cloud is never consulted and no offer is made at all. main.js:393 sets dirty=true for 'new'. save.js:276-297 save() writes the cloud unconditionally (last-writer-wins) once init has finished (it waits up to 4 s).
findings.suggested_fix: Track 'cloud unverified' at boot (timeout, or init not ready). Before the first cloud write in that session, read the doc and refuse/prompt if one exists that this session did not load (compare savedAt with a per-session base). Run the newer-save offer also when there is no local save (as a modal choice, not a 15 s toast). Keep a backup copy (e.g. doc 'slot1_prev' / localStorage morada:slot1.bak) before every overwrite. Do not mark a boot 'new' game dirty until the cloud check has completed.
findings.root_cause: main.js:329 races M.save.loadEntry against CLOUD_BOOT_WAIT=1500 ms (main.js:22). On timeout, entry is undefined. With no local mirror, main.js:337 returns {state:null, where:'new'}. offerNewerCloud is only reached when a local save exists (main.js:331-333). save.js:304 waits only INIT_WAIT_LOAD=1200 ms for capabilities; if init is not ready, cloudReady() is false and loadEntry returns null (save.js:305-309). readCloud also returns null on its own 2.5 s timeout (save.js:251). So 'no save exists' and 'cloud was never consulted' look identical to main.js. main.js:368 starts newGame. save.js:286-293 then waits up to 4 s for init and writes the cloud doc unconditionally (last writer wins). Note: dirty=true at main.js:379 is not the trigger, because frame() sets dirty=true on every frame in which sim time advances (main.js:167).
findings.vfix: Make loadEntry return {state, where, cloudChecked:boolean}, with cloudChecked false when init was not ready or the read timed out or failed. In main.js keep a session flag cloudVerified=false until a cloud read actually completes. Always run the late cloud check, also when there is no local save, and make it a modal choice instead of a toast. In save.js, guard writes: before the first cloud write of a session that has not verified the cloud, read the doc. If it exists and its savedAt is newer than the session's base savedAt (0 for a new game), do not overwrite it. Write to '<slot>_conflict' or ask the player instead. Keep a backup ('<slot>_prev' doc and localStorage morada:<slot>.bak) before each overwrite. Skipping the dirty flag alone will not help, because the loop re-sets it.

findings.title: No sofa nap at night: characters without a free bed faint on the floor instead of napping on a free sofa (workers get fired)
findings.repro: cd $GAME && node tools/qa_simeng_nosofanap.mjs → 'start 23:00 (no bed, free sofa) -> {talk 15, kiss 3.5, joke 8.5, dance 8 … _faint 77} fainted at 23:43' vs 'start 15:00 -> {nap 116}'. node tools/qa_simeng_scen.mjs four_starter (starter house + 2 members, one double bed): 18× 'desmaiou de cansaço' in 8 days, 'Caio faltou ao trabalho de novo e foi demitido(a)' on d3. node tools/qa_simeng_scen.mjs nobed --days 4: both faint every night, Caio fired d3 (missed carpools while fainted).
findings.expected: When no bed slot is available, an exhausted character naps or sleeps on a sofa or armchair, at least when energy is critical.
findings.actual: At night the nap interaction advertises nothing, so even the energy override (≤ −90) finds no candidate. Characters keep socialising until they hit −100 and faint for ~11 h.
findings.suspected_cause: data.js:173 AUTONOMY.napGate is −100 for 20:00–05:59. effectiveAds (engine.js:590-594) returns {} when energy > gate, which also empties the restricted overrideCritical → runAutonomy(sim,'energy') call.
findings.suggested_fix: Set napGate at night to about −60, or ignore the gate when no bed slot is free or when called from the critical override. Consider a 'Dormir no sofá' interaction.
findings.root_cause: data.js:173-174 AUTONOMY.napGate is -100 for hours 20-05. effectiveAds (engine.js:590-592) returns {} whenever energy > gate, which is always true because energy -100 triggers a faint first. The critical override (engine.js:2489-2510 → runAutonomy(sim,'energy')) therefore has no candidate once beds are full (hasCapacity false), and the character idles or socialises until it faints for about 11 h. A night faint lasts until about 16:00, so the 09:00 carpool is missed (wakeUp only cancels sleep/nap, engine.js:2706-2708).
findings.vfix: Set the night napGate to about -60/-70. Bed sleep (ad 84 × circadian 1) still beats a sofa nap whenever a bed slot is free. Alternatively pass a flag from overrideCritical so effectiveAds ignores the gates for restrict==='energy'. Consider a 'Dormir no sofá' interaction with a full-night duration. Optional: warn in the UI when household size exceeds bed slots.

findings.title: Night-shift jobs: no sleep before the shift → faint on the sidewalk for ~11 h after work; performance spiral; promote/demote loop
findings.repro: cd $GAME && node tools/qa_simeng_night.mjs 7 (Segurança 'Vigia noturno' 00–06): 'd2 23:39 energy -73 … foi para o trabalho' → 'd3 06:00 energy -100 … Lia desmaiou de cansaço!' (faint 11.1 h on d3 and again d10); perf 0 → -75 in 14 days with no missed shift. node tools/qa_simeng_energy.mjs (Ciência L2, 23–05, promoted right after a 09–15 shift): energy -75 at 22:40 departure, -100 at 05:00, _faint 05:00→16:20 at the mailbox tile (12,17). node tools/qa_simeng_scen.mjs single_job --days 21 --verbose: 'd4 Promoção… 23h–5h', 'd11 05:00 rebaixado', 'd11 15:00 Promoção' again, 'd19 rebaixado'.
findings.expected: A night-shift worker sleeps or naps in the evening (the alarm 2 h before the shift wakes them) and comes home tired but not collapsing. Performance follows mood.
findings.actual: Sleep is never chosen in the hours before the shift. The character works the night at energy −50…−75, the work drain pushes them to −100 on arrival, and they faint at the lot entrance for 11 h (losing the day). Mood at departure drops, performance falls, and at L2 they bounce between promotion and demotion.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:763 skips any candidate whose estMinutes is more than the minutes until work once that is under 180; sleep is estimated at 480 (engine.js:729), so sleep is impossible in the 3 h before a shift. sleepGate/circadian (data.js:156-176) block beds for the rest of the evening. returnFromWork applies the whole workDelta in one lump with no floor (engine.js:2794: energy −5/h × 6 h), so the faint is instant. The demotion branch resets performance to 0 (engine.js:2815-2819), and L2 has no requirements, so the next good shift re-promotes.
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt sleep/nap from the budget filter (the alarm already wakes them), or plan a pre-shift nap. Floor the return-from-work drain (e.g. energy ≥ −80, hunger ≥ −90). Add a cooldown after a demotion before another promotion check.
findings.root_cause: (1) engine.js:763: once minutesUntilWork < 180, any candidate with estMinutes > budget is skipped. Sleep is estimated at 480 (engine.js:729), so beds are excluded from 21:35 on before a 00:00 shift (22:35 for a 23:00 shift). (2) Before that window, sleepGate (data.js:171-172) requires energy ≤ -60/-60/-25 at 19/20/21 h, and circadian scales sleep ads by 0.06-0.35. (3) napGate is -100 for 20:00-05:59 (data.js:173-174), so no sofa nap is possible either. (4) returnFromWork applies workDelta × hours as one lump with no floor (engine.js:2794; Segurança energy -7.5/h × 6 h = -45), so arrival at ≤ -55 means an instant 11 h faint on the arrival tile. (5) Demotion resets performance to 0 (engine.js:2815-2819), and L2 has no requirements, so the next shift with mood > 0 re-promotes at 40%.
findings.vfix: Exempt sleep/nap from the budget filter at engine.js:763. The careerTick alarm and the 25-min auto-go already wake sleepers. Make sleepGate/circadian shift-aware: for a worker whose next shift starts between 20:00 and 02:00, treat the 4-6 h before the shift as night. Floor the return lump (energy and hunger ≥ -80), or spread it over the shift. Add a promotion cooldown (e.g. 3 shifts) after a demotion. Require performance > -20 for promotion rather than a 5% floor.

findings.title: With an older local save and a slow cloud, the newer cloud save is only offered in a 15 s toast; the next autosave overwrites it
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --wait 2500 --script tools/qa_cr_cloudrace.mjs (local mirror money 1111, cloud doc money 2222 saved later, cloud get 2.5 s) -> booted {money:1111, toasts:['Há um jogo salvo mais recente na nuvem (Dia 1). Carregar']}. The player does not click; autosave('day') -> cloudMoneyNow 1116, newerCloudSaveLost:true
findings.expected: Progress made on another device is never silently destroyed. Choosing between two saves should be an explicit, persistent choice.
findings.actual: The offer disappears after 15 s (ui.js:1037). Any autosave (new sim day, tab hidden, pagehide) replaces the newer cloud doc with the older local branch.
findings.suspected_cause: main.js:356-367 offerNewerCloud only shows ui.offer(). save.js:287-293 writeCloud has no compare-before-write or conflict guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the conflict a modal with both saves' family, day, money and time, and block cloud writes until it is resolved. Alternatively write to a conflict/backup doc instead of overwriting a cloud save newer than the session's base savedAt.
findings.root_cause: main.js:340-350 offerNewerCloud only calls ui.offer(), which has a 15 s timeout (ui.js:1037), and nothing blocks writes in the meantime. main.js:333 calls offerNewerCloud only when entry === undefined, i.e. when the boot race timed out. When loadEntry itself gives up on the cloud (init not ready after 1.2 s at save.js:304, or the read times out at save.js:251), it resolves with the local entry (save.js:305-311). main.js:330 then returns that entry directly, so no late check ever runs. save.js:286-293 writeCloud has no compare-before-write.
findings.vfix: Treat a boot that did not complete a cloud read as unverified, and always schedule the late check (retrying until init and the read succeed). Show the conflict as a persistent modal listing both saves (family, day, money, date), and suspend cloud writes for that slot until the player chooses. Add a savedAt guard in save(): remember the base savedAt loaded at boot. Before writing, read the doc, and if doc.savedAt > base, write to '<slot>_conflict' instead of overwriting, then notify the player.

findings.title: Food or a dirty plate on a counter or table can barely be clicked; clicking it reports "Nada para fazer aqui agora."
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_live_meal.mjs (and --touch --w 390 --h 844). The script puts a 3-serving meal on counter (16,11) and a dirty plate on the dining table. It samples a 13x13 grid over each tile's screen box with M.render.pick, then makes a real click on the item's visual centre. Desktop meal: count {counter:64, stove:33, tile:53, sim:13, TARGET:6}; the centre pick is the counter (id 111). Desktop plate: TARGET 3/169, and the centre click shows the tip "Nada para fazer aqui agora." (from the table). Phone (tile is 31x41 px): a centre click on the meal shows "Nada para fazer aqui agora.". Zoomed screenshot shots/qa/live/meal-desk-meal-zoom.png: the hover label reads "Balcão de cozinha" while the cursor is on the plates. tools/qa_live_mealray.js: a ray through (16.5,0.95,11.5) hits only the counter, because the middle of the plate cluster is empty counter top.
findings.expected: Clicking cooked food (or a dirty plate) on a counter or table opens its pie ("Pegar um prato e comer" / "Recolher prato").
findings.actual: The tiny plate meshes are the only pick target. Most clicks hit the counter or table, which have no interactions, so the player gets "Nada para fazer aqui agora." (or nothing). Telling a character to eat the meal they just cooked is a pixel hunt, and nearly impossible on a phone.
findings.suspected_cause: render.js:1824-1834. pick() returns the first raycast hit, and items on surfaces only have their small plate geometry. ui.js:1188/1198 (openPie) then finds no interactions on the counter or table.
findings.suggested_fix: In ui.js liveClick/openPie: when the picked object is a surface (def.surface), or has no interactions, check M.world.itemAt(p.x, p.y) using the tile pick already returns, and open that item's pie. Alternatively, give noBlock items an invisible pick proxy box covering their tile's top (or prefer items over their supporting surface in render.pick).
findings.root_cause: render.js:1825-1834: pick() returns the first raycast hit among object meshes. Meals and plates on surfaces are only small plate meshes, so most rays hit the supporting counter or table. ui.js:1188-1201 (openPie) then gets [] from getInteractions(counter/table) and shows the generic tip. ui.js:1116-1119 (updateHover) also labels the counter instead of the food.
findings.vfix: In ui.js liveClick/openPie (and updateHover), when the picked object's def is a surface or has no interactions, call M.world.itemAt(p.x, p.y). pick already returns the tile of the hit point. If an item is found, open that item's pie and show its label. Alternatively, have render.pick prefer an item on the hit surface tile.

findings.title: Accepting a newspaper job while employed wipes career progress in one click, with no confirmation
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_live_job.mjs. Caio is selected by portrait. As setup, his career is set to Negócios level 4 (performance 60). A real click on the newspaper, then on the pie item "Aceitar vaga: Garçom de bufê (Artes & Mídia) — M$ 100/dia". Output: careerBefore ["Negócios",4,"Executivo júnior"] → careerAfter ["Artes & Mídia",1,"Garçom de bufê"], confirmShown false, note "Caio agora trabalha como Garçom de bufê...".
findings.expected: Switching jobs warns that the current job and level will be lost. It should show the current vs new title, pay and hours and ask for confirmation, or at least label the item "Trocar de emprego".
findings.actual: The job is replaced at level 1 immediately. The pie label is also cut off (see LIVE-3), so the player may not even see that it is a lower-paid job in another career.
findings.suspected_cause: engine accept_job effect (availability at engine.js:557 only blocks the same track). The UI shows dynamic job:<track> items like any other interaction (ui.js onPieItem 1347).
findings.suggested_fix: For job:<track> items when sim.career exists, open a confirmation modal (ui.openModal) comparing the jobs, or move job acceptance into a dedicated offer card. Show a 'troca de emprego' hint in the label.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:557-559 availability only blocks the same track. engine.js:2627-2635 acceptJob overwrites sim.career. ui.js:1347 onPieItem queues job:<track> like any other item, with no confirmation branch.
findings.vfix: In ui.js onPieItem, for keys starting with 'job:' while the selected sim has a career, open an in-UI confirmation (ARCHITECTURE forbids confirm()). It should compare current title/level/pay with the new title/pay/hours. Also relabel the item 'Trocar de emprego: …' in engine getInter (engine.js:439-447) when sim.career exists.

findings.title: Walking characters are hard to click, and every miss sends the selected character walking
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_live_moving.mjs. Caio walks a long path at speed 1, and the script clicks his projected position 5 times. tries: pie opened 1/5. The instrumented pointerup picks were {kind:'tile'} 4 times and the selected Rita once (tip 'Rita Alves (selecionado)'). Note: the headless SwiftShader frame rate is low, which inflates the miss rate.
findings.expected: Clicking on or right next to a moving character opens their social pie.
findings.actual: The capsule is thin (radius 0.27 tiles ≈ 13 px at default zoom, ≈ 6 px on the phone camera), so most clicks on a walker miss. A miss is treated as a floor click and queues 'Andar até aqui' for the selected character.
findings.suspected_cause: render.js:1807 pickSim threshold `r.d < 0.27`. ui.js:1509-1514 liveClick turns any tile pick into queueWalk.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the capsule, at least for moving characters (about 0.45). In liveClick, before treating a pick as a tile, check for a character within about 0.6 tile of the ground point and prefer it.
findings.root_cause: render.js:1807 uses a fixed world-space capsule radius (r.d < 0.27). On narrow screens the camera distance is scaled up to 2.4x, so 0.27 world units is about 6 px each side. ui.js:1503-1515 picks at pointerup and turns any tile pick into queueWalk.
findings.vfix: Use a screen-space minimum radius in pickSim (for example max(0.27 world, ~16-22 px converted at the sim's depth), larger for touch and for moving rigs). In liveClick, before queueWalk, prefer a character whose feet are within ~0.6 tile of the ground point. Optionally use the pointerdown position or time for the pick.

findings.title: A full queue refuses actions silently, and walks are not capped
findings.repro: tools/qa_live_queue.mjs: queueing 9 snacks through the pie gives queueOverflow 8 and no notification (only an error beep). tools/qa_live_walkspam.mjs: 14 real floor clicks give walkQueueLen 13, but the strip shows only 8 (walkQueueDom 8, no '+5' indicator). Then 'Fazer um lanche' via the pie is not queued (afterSnackLen 13) and no message appears. Finishing the walks takes 24 sim-min.
findings.expected: The 8-action cap applies to walks too, or a new walk replaces the pending walk. A refused command explains why ('Fila cheia — cancele algo'). The strip shows a '+N' badge when more than 8 actions are queued.
findings.actual: Walks pile up without limit and are partly hidden. After that, every pie command fails with no visible reason.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:2311 queueWalk has no MAX_PLAYER_ACTIONS check. engine.js:2271/2301 return false without notify(). ui.js:607 refreshQueue renders only queue.slice(0, 8).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the cap (or the replace-pending-walk behaviour) to queueWalk. notify('Fila cheia (8 ações)') when the cap blocks a command. Render a '+N' chip in the queue strip.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:2309-2323 queueWalk has no MAX_PLAYER_ACTIONS check. engine.js:2271 and engine.js:2301 return false without notify(). ui.js:1347-1349 onPieItem only plays sfx('error'). ui.js:607 refreshQueue renders sim.queue.slice(0, 8) with no overflow indicator.
findings.vfix: Apply the cap in queueWalk, or replace the pending player walk. notify('Fila cheia (8 ações) — cancele algo', 'bad') or flashTip on refusal. Render a '+N' chip in the strip when queue.length > 8.

findings.title: Wallpaper is per edge, not per side: painting a room also paints the neighbouring room and the outside of the house
findings.repro: node tools/qa_vis_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --nofonts --script tools/qa_vis_states.mjs. The script calls E.paintWall('v,17,7', 6) for pink stripes on the bathroom's outer wall. shots/qa/vis/state-paint-outside.png shows the house exterior pink; state-paint-inside.png shows the bathroom interior pink. The starter house shows the same problem: h,7..11,10 is c=2 (sky blue) on both the living room and bedroom sides, and v,12,* is mustard on both the kitchen and living room sides (scene-1280x800-walls-k0-up.png vs walls-k2-up.png). The whole house looks randomly coloured.
findings.expected: DESIGN.md says 'wallpaper M$ 10/edge side'. Each face should be painted on its own, and the exterior should have a facade finish that does not change when the inside is decorated.
findings.actual: state.lot.walls[key] = {t, c} holds a single colour that is rendered on both faces. Applying 'Azulejo de banheiro' to a bathroom wall tiles the bedroom side and the street facade.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:3456 paintWall(edgeKey, idx) stores one c per edge. render.js:761 builds the wall slabs with one colour (e.color) for both faces.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a second colour field (e.g. c2 for the +x/+z side). The pick already returns the tile in front of the clicked face (render pick 'wall'), so paintWall can take a side. Build each body slab as two half-thickness boxes, or use per-face vertex colours. Give exterior faces (outdoor side) a default siding colour. Recolour the starter house so each room's paint stays inside that room.
findings.root_cause: The state shape walls[key]={t,c} has one colour per edge (ARCHITECTURE.md:65). engine.js:3456 paintWall(edgeKey, idx) writes that single c. render.js:761 builds e.color once, and render.js:799 body() uses it for the full-thickness slab, so both faces get it. world.js roomScore (notes/world.md:111) also scores 'wall sides' from the same c.
findings.vfix: Add an optional second colour field, e.g. c2 for the +x/+z face, defaulting to c so old saves keep working. render pick 'wall' already returns the tile in front of the clicked face, so the UI can pass a side and paintWall(edgeKey, idx, side) can write only that face. In render, split each body piece into two half-thickness boxes (-HT..0 and 0..HT) with their own colours, or use per-face vertex colours on the instanced box. Give outdoor-facing sides a default facade colour, and charge per side as DESIGN says. Recolour the starter house so each room's paint stays inside it.

findings.title: Any player command running at carpool time blocks going to work → missed work (and firing) while awake at home
findings.repro: cd $GAME && node tools/qa_simeng_carpool_player.mjs → for TV ('watch'), 'read' and 'shower' queued by the player at 08:20: 'queue at 08:36: watch/do/p50 > go/route/p40 | at 09:05 hidden(atWork)= false | … Caio perdeu a carona e faltou ao trabalho. Mais uma falta e será demitido(a)!'
findings.expected: DESIGN: the employed character goes to the carpool with priority when on the lot and awake. A running activity is interrupted at departure time, as with the alarm for sleep.
findings.actual: go_work is queued behind the player action, which runs past 09:00. Work is missed; two days in a row means fired.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:2733 sets the automatic go action to PRIO.urgent (40), which is lower than PRIO.player (50) (engine.js:14). enqueue (engine.js:801-828) inserts it after higher-priority actions, and nothing cancels the player action at autoGoBefore.
findings.suggested_fix: Give go_work a priority above player (e.g. 60), or cancel the running player action and drop queued player fillers when the 25-min auto-go fires. At minimum, warn the player.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:2733 queues the automatic carpool action at PRIO.urgent (40), below PRIO.player (50) (engine.js:14). enqueue (engine.js:801-828) inserts it behind every player action, and nothing interrupts a running player action at the 25-min auto-go point (careerTick, engine.js:2727-2735).
findings.vfix: In careerTick, set a.prio = PRIO.player + 1. enqueue then cancels the running player action gracefully (cur.cancel, idx 1), and later player commands queue behind go_work. Also refuse or warn when a player queues a 30+ min activity within about 60 min of a shift ('Caio precisa sair para o trabalho às 08:35').

findings.title: Characters stand inside a sofa or chair during a social when the request interrupts their last step onto the seat
findings.repro: cd $GAME && node tools/qa_simeng_trace.mjs --seed 5 --from "4 18:14" --to "4 18:24" → 'Rita@(8.00,12.00) walk [sit/enter > s:dance(R)/do]' then 'Rita@(8.00,12.00) dance [s:dance(R)/do]' (sofa_cheap occupies (8,12)). Screenshot: shots/qa/simeng/sofa_dance.png (node tools/integrate_check.mjs --nohelp --clear --eval tools/qa_simeng_shot_sofa.js --shot ../shots/qa/simeng/sofa_dance.png). Frequency: node tools/qa_simeng_default.mjs --days 10 --seeds 11,12,13,14,15,16 → insideBlock 13–42 half-minute samples in 4 of 6 seeds. Same with dining chairs: qa_simeng_scen.mjs single_job (Lia at (12.25,8) chair_wood dancing).
findings.expected: An interrupted walk or enter onto an on-slot (sofa, chair, bed) steps back to a free tile before the social starts.
findings.actual: The responder stays at the seat pose and dances or laughs inside the furniture for 4–15 min, then teleports out when the queue empties.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:1059 (walk-phase cancel → phase 'done') and engine.js:1067 (enter-phase cancel → 'done' unless already seated). The social respond (prio 40) sets cur.cancel via enqueue, so the action ends with the character on the blocked tile. stepRespond never moves them, and tickSim snaps them out only when the queue is empty (engine.js:2591-2594).
findings.suggested_fix: In the walk/enter cancel branches, go to phase 'exit' (using exitTarget/act.data.exit) when isOnBlocked(sim) or act.slot.on. Alternatively delay the respond until the partner is on a walkable tile.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:1067 (enter-phase cancel → 'done' because sim.seated is still false during enter) and engine.js:1059 (walk-phase cancel → 'done'). For on-slots the path's last node is the blocked furniture tile, and pushRespond (prio 40, engine.js:1963-1971) sets cur.cancel through enqueue. The action ends with the character on the blocked tile. stepRespond never moves them, and tickSim only snaps them to nearestWalkable once the queue is empty (engine.js:2591-2594), which shows as a teleport.
findings.vfix: In both cancel branches, if isOnBlocked(sim) or (act.slot && act.slot.on && act.progress >= act.path.length - 1), set act.phase = 'exit' (exitTarget uses act.data.exit = path[n-2]) instead of 'done'. Belt-and-braces: in stepSocial/stepRespond, if isOnBlocked(sim), step to nearestWalkable before the 'do' phase.

findings.title: Two characters occupy the same tile for 10–18 minutes (e.g. cooking inside a waiting housemate or guest)

findings.root_cause: freeSlots/slotHolder (engine.js:249-277) only respect a slot reserved by another character's queue head (useObjId + slotIdx). findings.expected: Performance follows mood at departure. Loneliness costs some mood but doesn't wipe 20 points every day.
findings.actual: With a positive mood (26–38) every day and no missed shift, performance drops about 12 per shift and the resident is demoted on day 11. They cannot fix social: no neighbours are known (empty-lot households start with 0 known, and walk-bys mostly happen while they're at work), and the phone requires known neighbours.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:2767 critAtDeparture = any motive except room ≤ −80 (social, fun and comfort included); engine.js:2802 applies −20.

findings.root_cause: engine.js:2767 critAtDeparture = any motive except room ≤ -80, including social, fun and comfort. engine.js:2802 subtracts 20, which outweighs the +8…+9 from a good mood. A lone resident's social decays without a fix: no known neighbours on an empty lot, walk-bys fall in walkbyStart-walkbyEnd 9-18 (data.js:944) while the worker is away, and the phone needs a known neighbour.
findings.vfix: Restrict critAtDeparture to hunger, energy, bladder and hygiene (or apply -5 for social/fun/comfort). Start empty-lot households with 1-2 known neighbours. Schedule walk-bys inside a window when a household member is home (e.g. after the shift or on days off).

findings.root_cause: engine.js:2389: hunger decay is purely proportional, 0.063 × (100 + hunger) per hour, so it approaches -100 asymptotically (about 0.11 left after 72 h). hospitalHunger = -100 (data.js:200) is tested with ≤ at engine.js:2464 and is unreachable from decay alone.
findings.vfix: Use hospitalHunger -99 (or ≤ -98.5). Alternatively add a small constant floor term to the hunger decay (e.g. max(0.5/h, proportional)), so starvation reaches the emergency after about a day at -95.

findings.expected: A study session lasts up to maxDuration (180 min), like the mirror speech, wherever the character sits.
findings.actual: The seat is preferred (standing slots get penalty 8), and the session ends as soon as comfort reaches the sofa cap. Skill gain per command drops by about 80%.
findings.suspected_cause: startDo engine.js:1106-1113 adds the seat's comfort rate to the study's rates. genericEnd engine.js:1178-1185 ends the action when every positive rate is capped; the study's own only rate is fun −6, so the seat comfort becomes the end condition.

findings.root_cause: startDo (engine.js:1106-1113) copies the seat's sit comfort rate and cap into act.rates/caps. genericEnd (engine.js:1178-1185) returns 'done' once every positive rate is capped. study_cooking/study_mechanical (data.js:673-677) have no positive rate of their own (only fun -6), so the seat's comfort cap becomes the end condition as soon as minDuration passes.
findings.vfix: Mark the seat comfort as passive (e.g. act.data.seatRate = 'comfort') and skip it in genericEnd's anyPos/canMore loop (and in canDeliver) unless the interaction itself has a positive comfort rate. Skill interactions then run to maxDuration or until mood/fun stops them.

findings.title: Social stall loop: when the target has a critical need nothing can fix, their response is cancelled every tick, freezing both characters for 12 minutes

findings.expected: Characters don't start socials with someone in a critical state, or the target simply declines once.
findings.actual: The initiator waits 12 min. The starving target is pulled into a respond action 24 times and can't do anything else (respond prio 40 beats her own actions).
findings.suspected_cause: overrideCritical engine.js:2501 cancels any respond action when the responder has a critical motive. canRespond (engine.js:1949-1961) and socialCandidates (669-706) don't exclude such targets, so stepSocial re-pushes the respond (engine.js:2077) until waited > 12.
findings.suggested_fix: canRespond returns 'no' when criticalMotive(t) is set, and socialCandidates skips targets in a critical state.
findings.root_cause: overrideCritical (engine.js:2501) cancels any respond action whenever the responder has a critical motive, before the overrideAt cooldown check, so it fires every tick. canRespond (engine.js:1949-1961) and socialCandidates (engine.js:669-706) do not exclude critical targets. stepSocial's enter phase (engine.js:2076-2079) re-pushes the respond every tick until waited > 12. Each push (prio 40) also cancels whatever auto action the target had just started, via enqueue.
findings.vfix: canRespond: return 'no' when criticalMotive(t) is set (the initiator fails at once with '… não pode agora'). socialCandidates: skip targets with criticalMotive(t). Optionally also skip initiators with a critical motive.

findings.title: Free will off: sleep/wake ping-pong (3-minute sleeps) ending in an 11-hour faint; hunger lump on return from work sends the worker to hospital
findings.repro: cd $GAME && node tools/qa_simeng_log.mjs nofreewill 7 4 Rita "sleep|faint|use|snack|cook|eat" → 'd2 22:11 sleep 6.5', '22:20 sleep 3.0', '22:27 sleep 3.0', '22:35 cook', '23:11 eat 4.5 (interrupted)', 'd2 23:15 -> d3 10:16 660.5 _faint'. node tools/qa_simeng_scen.mjs nofreewill --days 7 --verbose → Rita 33 sleeps totalling 1522 min plus 3 faints (1976 min); 'Caio desmaiou de fome e foi levado(a) para o atendimento de emergência' at 16:00 d3 and 15:00 d5, exactly when he returns from work.
findings.expected: With free will off, critical needs are handled (overrides) without oscillation. Returning from work never instantly hospitalises or faints someone.
findings.actual: Sleep ends after 1 minute because hunger ≤ −80. Food is only fetched at the −85 override, and hunger needs about 4 h to drift from −80 to −85 (proportional decay), so the energy override starts a new sleep every few minutes until the character faints. The work-return lump (hunger −5/h × 7 h) pushes hunger to −100 on arrival.
findings.suspected_cause: data.js:202-203 wakeHunger −80 and wakeBladder −80 are above overrideHunger −85 and overrideBladder −85. Sleep tick at engine.js:1369. Free-will-off branch of maybeAutonomy at engine.js:2538-2542. Lump without floor at engine.js:2794.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the thresholds (wake at the override value, or queue the hunger fix when sleep is cut by hunger). Floor work drain on return (e.g. hunger ≥ −90).
findings.root_cause: Sleep ends after 1 min when hunger ≤ wakeHunger -80 (engine.js:1369; data.js:203). Food is only fetched at overrideHunger -85 (data.js:202, criticalMotive engine.js:661-667). With proportional decay, -80 → -85 takes about 4.6 h, and in that band the free-will-off branch (engine.js:2538-2542) only sees energy ≤ -90 as critical. It re-queues sleep every 4-8 min, the sleep wakes at once, and eventually the character faints. Separately, returnFromWork applies hunger -5/h × 6-7 h as one unfloored lump (engine.js:2794), so leaving at ≤ about -65 means instant hospitalisation on arrival.
findings.vfix: Make wakeHunger/wakeBladder equal to the override thresholds (-85), or, when sleep is cut by hunger or bladder, queue runAutonomy(sim,'hunger'/'bladder') at PRIO.player+5 immediately. In criticalMotive, treat hunger ≤ wakeHunger as critical when energy is also critical. Floor the work-return lump (hunger and energy ≥ -80).

findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:3173-3179 collectorCheck stores amount and billIds in the collector's data at spawn. repossess (engine.js:3098-3116) uses sim.data.amount without checking which billIds are still in S.bills.

findings.root_cause: engine.js:3173-3179 collectorCheck captures amount and billIds at spawn. The collector walks to the doorstep (engine.js:3060-3075) and then calls repossess (engine.js:3098-3116). repossess uses sim.data.amount without checking which billIds are still unpaid in S.bills. Meanwhile pay_bills.finish (engine.js:1734-1747) can remove those bills.

Optionally let the household pay at the door (a pie entry on the collector) instead of losing objects.

findings.title: Engine cost grows superlinearly with object count; big houses cause hitches at fast speeds (world.ensure() re-hashes every object on every query)
findings.repro: node tools/qa_cr_scale.mjs (starter house + N extra purchased objects, 4 residents, 1 sim day): 31 objects 545 ms/sim-day; 91 -> 971 ms; 182 -> 8100 ms, worst single 0.5-min step 93 ms; 239 -> 13665 ms/sim-day (28.5% of a core at 30× ultra), worst step 61 ms. isWalkable calls/sim-day: 7k -> 61k -> 78k. Profile: node --cpu-prof tools/qa_cr_scale_prof.mjs -> objSig (world.js:299) 45.6% self time; objRoom (engine.js:176) 6.6%; roomAt (engine.js:159) ~10%.
findings.expected: Engine stays well under a frame budget for a large, furnished house; no single step should take several frames.
findings.actual: At about 180+ objects, single engine steps take 60–90 ms (4–6 dropped frames) and a sim day costs 8–14 s of CPU.
findings.suspected_cause: world.js:369-383 ensure() calls objSig(S.objects) (world.js:299-309, O(n)) at the top of every public query (isWalkable, roomAt, edgeBlocked, inBounds, getWall, objectAt, findPath...). The engine calls walkable()/roomAt() per slot per object in each autonomy run (engine.js:157-159, dataSlots 181-207, seatSlots 278-301, adjacentSlots 215-235). That makes autonomy roughly O(objects² × objects).
findings.suggested_fix: The engine already calls M.world.rebuild() on every object change (objectsChanged). Make ensure() cheap: check array identity + length + an explicit version counter, or compute objSig at most once per engine tick. Cache dataSlots/objRoom per object keyed by M.world.version. Optionally time-slice autonomy (one resident per tick).
findings.root_cause: world.js:369-383 ensure() runs objSig(S.objects) (world.js:298-309, O(n)) at the top of every public query (26 call sites: isWalkable, inBounds, roomAt, edgeBlocked, objectAt, findPath, ...). The engine issues these per slot per object in each autonomy pass. dataSlots, seatSlots and the walkable/roomAt wrappers are around engine.js:157-235 and 278-301. That makes one autonomy pass roughly O(objects^2), and the residual growth comes from routing over more candidates.
findings.vfix: The engine already calls M.world.rebuild() through objectsChanged() on every object mutation. Make ensure() O(1): check array identity + length + a mutation counter bumped by rebuild()/setWall/setFloor. Alternatively compute objSig at most once per engine update (e.g. M.world.beginFrame() called from engine.update). Also cache per-object slot lists and objRoom keyed by M.world.version, and time-slice autonomy (at most one resident's full autonomy pass per tick).

findings.root_cause: main.js:31 sets `let slot = 'slot1'`. It changes only in saveNow(slotArg) (main.js:207) and loadSlot (main.js:317), and is never persisted. M.main.setSlot (main.js:421) has no callers. pickInitialState (main.js:329/331) always reads the default slot. ui.js prefs (ui.js:115, morada.prefs) store no slot. The only slot indicator is '(atual)' inside the slots modal (ui.js:2431/2461).
findings.vfix: Persist the slot whenever it changes, e.g. prefs.slot in morada.prefs or a localStorage key 'morada:lastSlot', plus the cloud meta for cross-device use. At boot, read it, or pick the newest entry from M.save.list(), before pickInitialState. Show the current slot name in the save chip and in Opções. Consider labelling 'Salvar aqui' on another slot as 'Salvar como… (passa a ser o jogo atual)'.

findings.title: Paintings and mirrors on interior walls are invisible and unclickable in the default 'Paredes: Recortadas' mode
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_live_states.mjs → painting: {"cutaway/k0":"NOT clickable","up/k0":"clickable","down/k0":"NOT clickable","cutaway/k2":"NOT clickable","cutaway/k1":"NOT clickable"}. Screenshots: shots/qa/live/states-desk-painting-cutaway-k0.png (the living-room painting is missing) vs states-desk-painting-up-k0.png (the painting is visible on the wall facing the camera). qa_live_pies.mjs also reports painting_cheap as unclickable.
findings.expected: Decorations on the back wall of a room, facing the camera, stay visible and can be used ("Admirar") in the default wall mode.
findings.actual: Every interior wall is cut down in cutaway mode from every camera angle, so wall-mounted items on interior walls are hidden. The starter painting can only be reached by switching to 'Altas'.
findings.suspected_cause: render.js cutaway rule: it lowers every wall whose far side is an indoor tile, which covers every interior wall. Wall-mounted objects are then hidden while their wall is cut.
findings.suggested_fix: Only cut walls that occlude the camera's view of the room: cut a wall when the tile on the camera side is outside the viewed room, or use per-face logic. Alternatively, keep wall-mounted items visible and pickable at a lowered height on cut walls.
findings.root_cause: render.js:1079-1085 computeCut adds every edge whose far-side tile is indoor, which is always true for interior walls, so all interior walls drop to 0.4 in every rotation. render.js:1399-1402 then hides any wall-mounted group when edgeHeight < 1.95. The hidden mesh also fails visibleChain in pick (render.js:1826), so the painting cannot be clicked.
findings.vfix: In computeCut, keep full height on an interior edge whose camera-facing side carries a wall-mounted object facing the camera (unless the selected-sim trace needs it cut). Or stop hiding wall items on cut walls: draw them at the cut height or as a small flat marker, and keep them pickable.

findings.title: Door/Window/Wallpaper/Demolish only register on the 0.4-high cutaway stub; aiming just above snaps to an invisible interior grid edge
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_bb_build2.mjs → R.survey.southWall_h20_5 = {0:'h,20,5',0.1:'h,20,5',0.2:'h,20,5',0.3:'h,20,5',0.38:'h,20,5',0.45:'h,20,5',0.6:'v,20,4',0.9:'v,20,4',1.5:'h,19,4'}, stubPx: 16 (the target band is 16 px tall at default zoom). tools/qa_bb_build.mjs, which clicked at wall height 0.6/1.2, failed door.place, window.place, paper.drag and demolish.clickDoor with tip 'Precisa de uma parede'. Screenshot shots/qa/bb/build-desk-5-door-hover.png: a red ghost slab inside the room plus 'Precisa de uma parede' while the cursor is just above the front wall stub. The first qa_bb_family.mjs run hit the same thing: the bathroom door click at height 0.5 picked 'v,9,11', so no bathroom door, both characters' bladder hit −100, and the toilet, sink and shower were unreachable.
findings.expected: Pointing anywhere on or just above a visible (cut-down) wall targets that wall, at least for tools that need an existing wall.
findings.actual: Only a ~16 px strip works. Slightly above it the nearest ground grid line wins, even one with no wall, so the player sees an error inside the room.
findings.suspected_cause: js/render.js:1875-1905 pickEdge. When the ray misses the lowered wall mesh it takes the nearest ground edge within 0.35 tile (1886-1897), and it never prefers edges that have a wall. The ray above a 0.4 stub reaches the ground ~0.5 tile behind it.
findings.suggested_fix: For door, window, paper and demolish, search only edges that have walls (for example within ~0.6 tile of the ground point, or by intersecting the ray with full-height invisible proxies of cut walls). Alternatively, raise walls temporarily while these tools hover.
findings.root_cause: js/render.js:1875-1905 pickEdge. The first branch (raycastWalls, about lines 1880-1884) works only while the ray actually hits the lowered 0.4 mesh. Once the ray passes over the stub, the ground point lands about 0.35+ tile behind the wall. The ground branch (about lines 1886-1898) then takes the nearest grid edge within 0.35 tile, with no preference for edges that hold a wall. showEdgeGhost (render.js:1986) draws full-height slabs, which makes the mismatch worse.
findings.vfix: Add a walls-only mode to pickEdge and use it from ui.js edgeAt for door, window, paper and demolish. Two options: (a) intersect the ray with invisible full-height (WALL_H) proxies for every existing wall edge, which matches the ghost slab; or (b) among ground candidates within about 0.6 tile, consider only edges where getWall(key) is set. Option (a) also fixes the phone tap target.

findings.root_cause: js/render.js:1821-1822. pick() returns pickSim(ray) before the object and wall raycast (1824-1828), and raySegment's t is never compared with wallHit.distance or objHit.distance. js/ui.js:1893-1903 buyClick calls deselectObject() for any non-object pick.
findings.vfix: In pick(), compute wallHit first and return the sim only if sim.t < wallHit.distance - 0.02 (the ray direction is normalized, so t is a distance). Add pick(x, y, {objectsOnly:true}) for buyClick and demolishClick that skips pickSim, so Buy and Build always select the furniture under the cursor.

findings.title: Lamp point lights leak through walls: bright green halos on the lawn outside the house at night
findings.repro: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-iastalker/022ed161-997d-54de-8293-6b75c8c0dc6f/scratchpad/game && node tools/qa_vis_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --nofonts --script tools/qa_vis_night.mjs → shots/qa/vis/night-westwall-2230.png (lamp 121 at 7,13 lights a ~3-tile green disc on the grass outside the west wall), night-house-2230-up.png (halos all around the house with walls up), night-bedroom-2230-k2.png, night-grass-0300.png. Also visible in the default view at 22:00: scene-1280x800-time-2200.png, the glow at about (300,380) left of the living room and at (1000,380) right of the shower.
findings.expected: Lamp light stays inside its room, and the outside wall faces and lawn stay dark.
findings.actual: Point lights (distance 4.3, no shadows) light everything within range, including grass and exterior walls through solid walls, and also rooms on the other side of interior walls.
findings.suspected_cause: render.js:301 creates a pool of 8 PointLights with castShadow=false. updateLamps (render.js:1411) puts them at lamp positions with no occlusion or room masking, and the ground plane (render.js:477) and wall body material receive every point light.
findings.suggested_fix: Cheapest fix: make the outdoor ground, the sidewalk and the exterior wall faces ignore point lights (separate material with point lights stripped via onBeforeCompile, or lights:false on a custom material), and shorten the distance to about 3.2. Better fix: mask by region. render.js already computes regions, so bake a per-tile region-id DataTexture, give each lamp its region id, and multiply the point-light contribution by (fragRegion == lampRegion) in a patched lights_fragment chunk.
findings.root_cause: js/render.js:300 creates 8 PointLights (0xffc98a, distance 4.3, decay 2) with castShadow=false. updateLamps (js/render.js:1411-1433) moves them to the lamp positions with no occlusion or room mask. The ground MeshStandardMaterial (js/render.js:477) and the instanced wall bodies receive every point light, so light passes through walls onto the lawn, the outer wall faces and neighbouring rooms.
findings.vfix: Cheap fix: patch the ground, sidewalk and wall materials with onBeforeCompile so they skip the point-light loop. three r128 has no per-light layers. Then shorten the distance to about 3.0-3.2. Better fix: bake a per-tile region-id DataTexture from S.regions, which render already computes, and pass each lamp's region as a uniform. In a patched lights_fragment chunk, multiply each point light by (fragRegion == lampRegion). Outdoor tiles get region 0, so they never receive indoor lamps.

findings.title: An unreadable save (one null entry in npcs/notifications/events, or version > 1) is silently replaced by a new game and destroyed by the next autosave
findings.repro: node tools/qa_cr_sanitize.mjs -> 'npcs:[null]', 'notifications:[null]', 'events:[null]': passesValidate true, initThrows "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'id')" (bills/objects/sims/queue nulls are handled). Browser: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --wait 2500 --script tools/qa_cr_badsave.mjs -> for nullEntry and newerVersion: booted {household:'Família Alves', money:6500, dirty:true}, toasts:[], originalSaveSurvived:false after one autosave. Console: "[Morada] save inválido, começando um jogo novo TypeError ... at sanitizeState".
findings.expected: Tolerate or strip bad entries. If a save truly cannot be loaded (corrupt, or made by a newer build), tell the player, offer export, and never autosave over it.
findings.actual: No message; the starter family appears; the next tab-hide or day-change autosave overwrites the only copy. A save written by a newer version of the game is wiped by an older cached build the same way.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:3755-3764 sanitizeState loops st.npcs / st.notifications / st.events and dereferences entries without filtering non-objects. save.js:85-98 validateState does not check these arrays, and rejects version>1 (save.js:87) by returning null, which loadEntry reports as 'no save'. main.js:383-388 restart catches the engine.init failure and falls through to newGame with dirty=true (main.js:393).
findings.suggested_fix: Filter non-object entries in sanitizeState (`st.npcs = st.npcs.filter(n => n && typeof n === 'object')`, same for notifications/events). In restart/loadEntry, distinguish 'no save' from 'save present but unreadable/newer': copy it to morada:<slot>.broken, show a toast with Export/Recarregar, and switch autosave to a different slot (or keep dirty=false) so it is not overwritten.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:3755-3761 (`for (const n of st.npcs) { if (n.id == null)...`) and engine.js:3763-3764 (`see(n.id)` / `see(e.id)` for notifications/events) dereference entries without filtering. Objects, bills and sims are filtered at 3730/3734/3765. save.js:85-98 validateState does not check these arrays. save.js:87 rejects version > 1 by returning null, and parseBody/loadEntry then report that as 'no save'. main.js:364-368 catches the engine.init error and falls through to newGame with no UI message. The next autosave (main.js:195-200) replaces the only copy.
findings.vfix: In sanitizeState add `st.npcs = st.npcs.filter(n => n && typeof n === 'object')`, and do the same for notifications and events, plus the per-sim relationships/lockouts values. In save.js, distinguish 'absent' from 'present but unreadable or newer' (return {state:null, unreadable:true, raw}). In main.js restart, when the save is unreadable: copy it to morada:<slot>.broken (and to a cloud '<slot>_broken' doc), show a toast or modal with Exportar / Recarregar, and switch to another slot (or disable autosave for this slot) so it is never overwritten silently.

findings.root_cause: engine.js:3098-3116 repossess: takes objects sorted by refund value, most valuable first, until taken ≥ amount (3106), then always removes all the overdue bills (3113), regardless of what was taken.

findings.title: Social initiators stand idle 10–12 minutes waiting for a busy partner (cooking/eating/toilet)
findings.repro: cd $GAME && node tools/qa_simeng_socwait.mjs → 'default Rita Alves: 19 min/day waiting in social enter … Caio Alves: 13 min/day'; four_empty 7–22 min/day per character. findings.expected: Give up quickly (1–2 min) or pick a different activity when the partner becomes busy.
findings.actual: About 15–20 min/day per character of standing still in front of a busy partner, which also feeds the overlaps in SIM-7.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:2070-2079 waits up to 10 (busy) or 12 (respond not yet active) sim-minutes before failing.

With the respond not yet active it waits up to 12. Both are long relative to how likely the partner is to come free, and the initiator stands still the whole time.
findings.vfix: Fail after about 2 sim-min when the partner's head action is a busy effect with more than a few minutes left (check elapsed against duration or estMinutes), and lock that social or partner pair for about 30 min. Let the initiator pick another activity instead of standing.

findings.title: The low-mood refusal says 'Cuide de: Diversão' while every fun or social action is disabled
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_live_sleep.mjs. Rita's motives are set to hunger/energy/bladder/hygiene -40, comfort -60, fun -100, social -95, room -100 (mood -64). A real click on the TV gives the pie ["-Assistir TV [De mau humor demais.]"]. Trying the command gives the toast "Rita está de mau humor e se recusa. Cuide de: Diversão."
findings.expected: When the game advises fixing a motive, the actions that fix it are allowed. Fun and social are needs.
findings.actual: The game tells the player to take care of Diversão (or Social) but refuses every TV, stereo or social command. The player has to fix unrelated needs or wait for free will.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:16 NEED_MOTIVES = ['hunger','energy','bladder','hygiene','comfort'] (fun and social are missing), used by isNeedInter (472). engine.js:2265-2268 builds the advice from lowestMotive over all 8 motives. getSocials (2374) refuses all socials below refuseMood.
findings.suggested_fix: Count fun and social interactions as need actions when that motive is the lowest or below about -50. Or restrict the advice to motives the player can actually act on.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:16 NEED_MOTIVES excludes fun and social, and isNeedInter (engine.js:472-480) uses it for the refusal checks at engine.js:2265 and 2353. getSocials refuses everything at engine.js:2374. The advice and thought bubble come from lowestMotive (engine.js:348-356), which ranks fun and social. The UI labels all 8 motives as 'Necessidades'.
findings.vfix: Treat an interaction as a need action when it raises the sim's currently lowest motive (or any motive below -50), including fun and social. Alternatively, make the refusal tip and thought bubble name only motives the player can still act on.

findings.title: Moving or selling an object in use leaves the character sitting or showering in mid-air while Buy mode is open
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_bb_misc.mjs: Rita sits on the sofa, then Buy, select sofa, Mover, click (10,16). Result: sofa at [10,16,2], Rita still at [8,12] with anim 'sit', seated:true, queue 'Sentar:exit:cancel' (shots/qa/bb/misc-desk-1-sofa-moved-paused.png shows her sitting on nothing). In tools/qa_bb_occl.mjs, selling the shower in use leaves Caio at [16,6] with anim 'shower' until Live resumes. He then recovers to idle at (16,7).
findings.expected: The character stands up or snaps to a free tile right away, or the move/sale is refused as 'Em uso'.
findings.actual: The pose persists for as long as Buy or Build stays open, because time is paused.
findings.suspected_cause: js/engine.js:3117-3126 cancelUsersOf only switches the action to phase 'exit'. The exit runs only when time advances, and Buy/Build pause the simulation. relocateSims (engine.js:3333) skips this case because the tile became walkable.
findings.suggested_fix: When an object is moved or sold, finish the users' exit at once: set anim 'idle', seated/asleep false, and move them to nearestWalkable. Or disallow moving or selling objects in use, with a tip.
findings.root_cause: js/engine.js:3117-3126 cancelUsersOf only switches a started action to phase 'exit'. The exit runs in tick(), which Buy and Build never call. relocateSims (engine.js:3334-3346) does nothing because the old tile is now walkable. moveObject (3385) and sellObject (3373) rely on that path.
findings.vfix: Add an immediate exit in cancelUsersOf (or a flag passed by moveObject/sellObject). For users whose phase was 'do' or 'enter': set anim 'idle', seated=false and asleep=false, pop the action and run cancelHooks, then snap them to WO().nearestWalkable(s.x, s.y). Or refuse the move or sale with a tip such as 'Em uso por Rita'.

findings.title: Starter house furniture resells at 100% on day 1 (M$ 4.825 of free cash)

findings.expected: Starter furniture is already used, so the depreciated value applies.
findings.actual: Selling the starter furniture on day 1 raises cash from M$ 6.500 to M$ 11.325.

findings.title: Cancelling 'Preparar refeição' at the fridge or counter never refunds the food money (also when fridge/counter/stove is sold or moved mid-cook)
findings.repro: node tools/qa_cr_cookrefund.mjs -> 'cancel via queue (control)' at stage 1 do-phase: paidForFood 30, refundedFood 0, meals 0. Same for 'sell fridge during stage 0', 'sell counter during stage 1', 'move counter during stage 1' (refundedFood 0, no meal).
findings.expected: cook_meal.cancel (engine.js:1538-1543) clearly intends a refund while stage <= 1 and nothing has been placed.
findings.actual: The money is lost: the cancel hook is never called for actions cancelled in their 'do' phase, which is where the sim spends almost all of stages 0/1.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:1124 doPhase handles act.cancel with endDo(...,false) -> 'exit' -> eff.finish(); cook_meal.finish is a no-op (engine.js:1544). cancelHooks (engine.js:829-841) only runs for route/walk/enter cancellation, queue drops and failAction. cancelUsersOf (engine.js:3121) sets noFinish and skips hooks entirely for the head action.
findings.suggested_fix: In cook_meal.finish: `if (!completed) EFFECTS.cook_meal.cancel(sim, act);`. In cancelUsersOf, call cancelHooks(s, a) for the head action too.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:1124 doPhase handles act.cancel with endDo(...,false), so the action goes to 'exit', then eff.finish (engine.js:1081), and cook_meal.finish is a no-op (engine.js:1543). cook_meal.cancel (engine.js:1537-1542), which refunds while stage <= 1, runs only from cancelHooks, i.e. route/walk/enter cancels, queue drops and failAction (engine.js:829-841). cancelUsersOf (engine.js:3117-3125), used by sellObject and moveObject, sets noFinish for a started head action and skips both finish and cancelHooks.
findings.vfix: `finish(sim, act, it, completed) { if (!completed) EFFECTS.cook_meal.cancel(sim, act); }` and in cancelUsersOf call cancelHooks(s, a) for the started head action as well (the cancel hooks are idempotent via act.data.paid = 0).

findings.title: Red 'Dinheiro insuficiente para pagar as contas.' alert when the bills were already paid by someone else
findings.repro: node tools/qa_cr_paytwice.mjs (both residents queue 'Pagar contas' for one M$ 120 bill) -> money 4880, bills 0, notifications: 'money: Rita pagou 1 conta (M$ 120).', 'bad: Dinheiro insuficiente para pagar as contas.' (with M$ 4.880 in the bank). Also in qa_cr_collector2 output after the collector cleared the bills.
findings.expected: No error, or 'As contas já estavam pagas.'
findings.actual: A 'bad' toast plus error sound claiming the family is broke.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:1734-1747 pay_bills.finish: when count === 0 it always notifies insufficient money, even when S.bills is empty. The 'hasBills' requirement is only checked at queue time (availability), not when the queued action starts.
findings.suggested_fix: `if (!S.bills.length) { notify('As contas já estavam pagas.', 'info'); return; }`. More generally, re-check `requires` when an action leaves the 'route' phase and drop chores that are no longer needed.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:1734-1747 pay_bills.finish notifies 'Dinheiro insuficiente' whenever count === 0, including when S.bills is already empty. The 'hasBills' requirement is checked only at queue and availability time, not when a queued action reaches the object or starts 'do'.
findings.vfix: At the top of pay_bills.finish: `if (!S.bills.length) { notify('As contas já estavam pagas.', 'info'); return; }`. More generally, re-check it.requires (checkRequires) when an action leaves 'route' or enters 'do', and drop chores that no longer apply without a 'bad' toast.

findings.title: Hug and kiss interpenetrate: torsos overlap and heads merge
findings.repro: node tools/qa_vis_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --nofonts --script tools/qa_vis_chars.mjs → shots/qa/vis/char-soc-hug.png and char-soc-kiss.png. The partners are 1.00 tile apart and each steps 0.3/0.33 toward the other, so Caio's head ends up inside Rita's.
findings.expected: The arms wrap around the partner and the bodies touch without passing through each other.
findings.actual: The centres end up about 0.35 apart, so torsos and heads intersect visibly.
findings.suspected_cause: models.js:2188-2200 hug P.pz=0.3 and kiss P.pz=0.33 are fixed and ignore the partner distance. engine socialSpacing keeps partners about 1 tile apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the partner distance in the animate ctx and use pz = max(0, (dist - 0.62) / 2). Or have the engine glide the pair to about 0.65 tile for hug/kiss and use pz ≈ 0.
findings.root_cause: models.js:2190 hug P.pz=0.3 and models.js:2197 kiss P.pz=0.33 (plus srx/nrx forward lean) are fixed offsets. engine socialSpacing (engine.js:2016) keeps the pair about 1 tile apart, and the anim ignores the actual partner distance.
findings.vfix: Pass the partner distance in the animate ctx (render knows both sims) and solve for pz: kiss pz ≈ max(0, (dist - 0.34)/2) - lean so head centres end about 0.29 apart (≈0.25 at dist 1.0); hug pz ≈ 0.27 with the existing nrz head tilt. Or have the engine glide the pair to about 0.6 tile for hug/kiss and use pz ≈ 0.

findings.title: A newly walled room with no floor renders as a closed full-height box and counts as outdoor, so the player builds blind
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_bb_build.mjs → room.detected {area:9, indoor:false, score:−15}. Screenshot shots/qa/bb/build-desk-3-diag.png: the 3x3 room is an opaque white box in cutaway mode, with only a sliver of grass visible inside. After the floor drag it becomes indoor (score −8) and the walls cut down.
findings.expected: Any enclosed area is treated as a room for cutaway and is visible, or the UI explains that it needs a floor.
findings.actual: The walls stay full height until the room is mostly floored. Floor and furniture have to be placed through the walls.
findings.suspected_cause: js/world.js:1310 indoor = !leak && !(grass*2 > area). js/render.js:709 uses the same rule for cutaway regions.
findings.suggested_fix: For cutaway, use enclosed (!leak) only. Or show a tip like 'Cômodo fechado — coloque piso para ele contar como interior'.
findings.root_cause: js/render.js:709 computeRegions marks a region indoor only if !leaks && grass*2 <= count, and computeCut (render.js:1079-1085) cuts only walls whose far tile is indoor. This mirrors js/world.js:1310.
findings.vfix: Store an 'enclosed' flag (!leaks) per region in computeRegions. In computeCut, cut walls whose far tile is enclosed (or enclosed while in Build mode), and keep the grass rule only for room scoring. Optionally show the tip 'Cômodo fechado — coloque piso para contar como interior'.

findings.title: Character ground shadow stays 0.7 tile behind characters at the computer, piano and chess (dark smudge behind the chair)

findings.title: 'Relaxar' on a bed looks exactly like sleeping under the blanket; armchair nap looks exactly like sitting
findings.repro: tools/qa_vis_acts.mjs → shots/qa/vis/sheet-act-01.png (bed_single-relax vs bed_single-sleep are identical, and the double/lux beds the same) and sheet-act-00.png (armchair-nap is upright like sit).

Add an 'armchair' support kind, or a recline flag in the armchair model meta, so the nap leans the torso back about 35° and raises the legs.

findings.title: Buy-mode ghost leaks one hidden InstancedMesh per catalog-item switch
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --wait 2500 --eval tools/qa_cr_leaks.js -> ghost group children 0 -> 61 after 60 R.showGhost type switches (sceneNodes 290 -> 358). They are never released (still 61 after 4 newGame cycles and 90 buy/sell cycles). No other leaks: geometries/textures stable at 120/9 across new games, buy/sell and visitor churn.
findings.expected: Switching the item being placed replaces the ghost.
findings.actual: The old footprint InstancedMesh stays in the scene graph forever (invisible), growing with every item the player clicks in the catalog.
findings.suspected_cause: render.js:1923-1935 showGhost: on a type change it calls S.groups.ghost.remove(S.ghost.group) but never removes or disposes S.ghost.tiles. ensureInstanced (render.js:1974-1976) also drops old InstancedMeshes without dispose().
findings.suggested_fix: `if (S.ghost) { S.groups.ghost.remove(S.ghost.group); S.groups.ghost.remove(S.ghost.tiles); if (S.ghost.tiles.dispose) S.ghost.tiles.dispose(); }`, and dispose the replaced mesh in ensureInstanced.
findings.root_cause: render.js:1923-1935 showGhost: on a type change it removes S.ghost.group from S.groups.ghost but never removes or disposes S.ghost.tiles. ensureInstanced (render.js:1972-1985) also drops replaced InstancedMeshes without dispose().
findings.vfix: `if (S.ghost) { S.groups.ghost.remove(S.ghost.group); S.groups.ghost.remove(S.ghost.tiles); S.ghost.tiles.dispose && S.ghost.tiles.dispose(); }`. Better: keep a single tiles InstancedMesh with capacity = the largest footprint (e.g. 4) and reuse it across types. In ensureInstanced, call im.dispose() on the replaced mesh.

findings.title: Save→load mid-action teleports a character who was stepping onto a bed or sofa, or responding to a social inside furniture
findings.repro: cd $GAME && node tools/qa_simeng_default.mjs --days 8 --seeds 1,2 --saveload 37 → saveLoadIssues: 'sim moved on load … from [8,7.08] to [9,7] q relax/walk' and 'from [8.27,12.07] to [8,11] q dance/do'. 311 cycles per run otherwise clean (no exceptions, no NaN).
findings.expected: Loading keeps the character where it was, mid-step onto the slot.
findings.actual: init() pushes the character to the nearest walkable tile and re-routes, so a visible teleport happens after every load in those states.
findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:3817-3827 init() only exempts on-slot actions in the do/enter/exit phases. A walk-phase action whose final tile is the on-slot, and responders stuck inside furniture (SIM-6), get moved.
findings.suggested_fix: Also exempt act.phase === 'walk' with act.slot.on when the character is on the slot tile or the last path step. Fixing SIM-6 removes the second case.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:3817-3827 init() exempts only on-slot actions in the do/enter/exit phases. A walk-phase action whose current or last path node is the on-slot tile, and responders left inside furniture by SIM-6, are moved to nearestWalkable, and the walk is reset to 'route'.
findings.vfix: Also exempt a.phase === 'walk' && a.slot && a.slot.on when simTile equals the slot tile or the last path node; there, continue to 'enter' instead of 're-route'. Fixing SIM-6 removes the responder case.

findings.title: Double-tapping a portrait on touch does not centre the camera, although the help card says it does
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --touch --w 390 --h 844 --script tools/qa_live_touch.mjs → doubleTapPortrait {camMoved: 0, events: ['click','click']}. Two taps 80 ms apart produced two clicks and no dblclick. The touch help card says 'Toque para trocar de morador; toque duas vezes para centralizar.'
findings.expected: A double tap on a portrait selects that character and focuses the camera on them.
findings.actual: Only the selection happens. The camera never moves, because the browser does not send a dblclick for taps (iOS Safari also does not reliably send one).
findings.suspected_cause: ui.js:570 relies on the 'dblclick' event for the portrait buttons.
findings.suggested_fix: Detect a double tap in the portrait click handler: a second click on the same portrait within about 350 ms. Or focus on every tap of the already-selected portrait.
findings.root_cause: ui.js:570 relies only on the 'dblclick' event for portrait focus. A single tap (ui.js:569) only selects.
findings.vfix: In the portrait click handler, focus the camera when the clicked portrait is already the selected sim, or detect a second click on the same portrait within ~350 ms. Keep dblclick for mouse.

findings.title: Phone: the toast stack covers the top third of the screen, including the camera rotate button

findings.title: After a door or window is placed, the success tip is replaced within 30 ms by a red error tip
findings.repro: node tools/integrate_check.mjs --clear --nohelp --script tools/qa_bb_misc2.mjs → R.doorTipSeq: 0 ms 'M$ 115 · Porta instalada', 60 ms 'Precisa de uma parede' (bad:true), 250 ms still red. On phone: tools/qa_bb_touch.mjs with --touch --w 390 --h 844 shows a red 'Já é uma porta' tip right after a successful door tap (shots/qa/bb/touch-phone-8-door.png).
findings.expected: The confirmation stays visible for its ~1.8 s.

findings.suspected_cause: js/ui.js:2259 placeOpening runs setTimeout(() => buildHover(...), 30), which calls showTip(..., bad=true) and replaces the flashTip.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the re-hover until the flash expires, or show 'already a door' as a neutral (non-red) note.
findings.root_cause: js/ui.js:2259 placeOpening calls setTimeout(() => buildHover(ui.mouse.x, ui.mouse.y), 30). buildHover (ui.js:2219) sets reason 'Já é uma porta/janela' at ui.js:2234 and calls showTip(..., true), which overwrites flashTip's content without respecting its 1.8 s timer.
findings.vfix: Record ui._flashUntil = now + 1800 in flashTip and make buildHover update only the ghost (not the tip) while the flash is active. Also show 'Já é uma porta' as a neutral note (bad=false), since it is a state, not an error.

findings.title: Phone pie: the object title pill is covered by the item column, and long labels are truncated with the price lost

findings.title: Buy mode deletes puddles, dirty/spoiled plates, spoiled meals and the newspaper for free (bypasses chores and the maid)

findings.suspected_cause: engine.js:3373-3384 sellObject only refuses mailbox/carpool. ui.js:1893-1902 buyClick selects any picked object. ui.js:1983 offers 'Remover' for value-0 objects.
findings.suggested_fix: Ignore def.buyable === false objects in buyClick (allow 'Mover' only for the mailbox) and refuse them in sellObject.
findings.root_cause: engine.js:3373-3384 sellObject refuses only mailbox and carpool. ui.js:1893-1902 buyClick selects any picked object. renderToolbar (ui.js:1962-1975) offers 'Mover' and 'Remover' for any non-fixed object, including buyable:false items (moving a puddle or meal is also allowed).
